newsitem.title: UK: Utd Utilities gains, NatWest positive.
newsitem.headline: Utd Utilities gains, NatWest positive.

text.p: United Utilities Plc shares rose on Tuesday as NatWest recommended the stock and as water and electricity stocks extended recent gains on hopes a threatened "windfall" tax will not be as harsh as previously feared.

Sources said NatWest analysts highlighted United Utilities in a review of the water sector, though further details were not immediately available. NatWest analysts could not initially be reached for comment.
United Utilities shares were up 8p at 682-1/2 by 0756 GMT -- near their year's high of 696p set February 7 -- in modest volume of 70,117 shares.
Other water stocks also rose with Severn Trent Water Plc up 7p at 739-1/2 and Thames Water Plc up 5p at 682-1/2.

Among electricity stocks, National Power Plc was up 8p at 543, PowerGen Plc was up 7-1/2p at 646, The Energy Group Plc was up 7p at 502-1/2, Southern Electric Plc was up 3p at 431-1/2 and Scottish Power Plc was up 8p at 388.

Dealers said utility stocks continued to be in demand for their high yields and on hopes that the windfall tax planned by the opposition Labour party, well placed to win the May 1 election, will not be as heavy as some had expected.
With exporting stocks continuing to be squeezed by the strong pound, utilities also offered the appeal of largely domestic earnings, they said.
"They have been good and they are going to go better," said one dealer, "they are domestic plays, their yields are quite safe and we are seeing some buyers."

Utility shares kicked off recent gains last week after reports that Labour leader Tony Blair aimed to raise between three and five billion stg from the windfall tax, less than finance spokesman Gordon Brown had been aiming for.
Water stocks were also boosted last week by a recommendation from analysts at Schroder Securities.
NatWest also gave National Power and PowerGen a push last week, saying they offered "outstanding value" unless they were badly hit by the windfall tax.
